The stream of Asturias and Leon, the Christian kingdom of Spain, with Pelagius and Alfonso.
A battle scene captioned "Battle of Tours, Oct. 10th 732." The chart says Charles Martel defeated the Saracens there and saved Europe from them.

A drawing of the Kaaba at Mecca, which the chart calls the "Ka'aba or Temple." Its caption says it is claimed to have been built by Abraham, and that it is 40 miles from the Red Sea and half a mile around.
The stream "Mahometan Spain", from 714; the Saracens in Spain became emirs, then kings called the Ommiades.
Carloman abdicates and Pepin le Bref becomes king of all France, 22 years.
Almansor, the caliph, 21 years from 754 (Saffah dynasty of the Abbasides).
A note: "Extinction of the Lombard kingdom, 774."
Ragnor Lodbrog in the Danish stream.
Red ring: the VIIth Council, at Nice, Bithynia, September 24 to October 23, 787, against the iconoclasts (image breakers).
Offa, king in the Saxon Heptarchy, 39 years.
The Saracen Empire with the caliphs, from Yezid; a branch becomes the caliphs of Cordova from 755.
Adrian, the 97th pope, 23 years.
Charlemagne, "Charles the Great", son of Pepin, crowned Emperor of the West by Pope Leo in 800, called the strongest man of his time; reigned 46 years.
Irene, empress of the Eastern Empire, 10 years.
Leo III, the 98th pope, 20 years (to 816).
Abdallah or Al-Mamun, the caliph, 20 years (to 833).
A note that Oxford University was founded by Alfred the Great in 886 and Cambridge University about 630, restored by Edward in 915.
A portrait of Harun al-Rashid, the caliph of Baghdad, seated on a carpet, labeled "25th Caliph."
Louis I, "le Debonnaire", son, an inglorious and turbulent reign, 26 years.
Egbert, called the sole monarch of England, who the chart says ruled 38 years and became king of all England in 827.
The heading of the stream of the popes, "Papal Rome", with each pope numbered.
A note in the British stream: "795 The Normans and Danes invade." Below it the chart says the land was called England from 829.
A castle on a hill captioned "Feudal System. Existed from the 7th to the 11th century."
A scene of people being burned alive while a crowd of churchmen looks on, captioned "Burning alive, witches, etc. Martyrdom."
The stream of the Greek or Eastern Empire, with Leo VI, Theophilus, Michael III, Basil I and Leo VI the Philosopher.
Ruric, 16 years from 862, first of the Dukes of Russia.
Red ring: the VIIIth Council at Constantinople, October 5, 869 to February 28, 870.
Basil I, "the Greek", 19 years, from 867 to 886.
A crowned portrait of Otto I, "Otho the Great of Germany."
Alfred, "the Great", a prosperous reign, age 52, reigned 30 years (to 901).
Harold "Harfager" or "Fair-haired", king of Norway.
Athelstan, son of Edward, reigned 15 years from 925.
A note that Venice had 122 doges, the first Anafesto in 697 and the last Luigi in 1797, when Bonaparte gave it to Austria.
A long table of the main European battles since AD 1500, from Tewkesbury and Bosworth to the Russo-Turkish War of 1877-78, each with its date.
Hugh Capet, first of the Capetian kings of France, 9 years.
Wladimir I, "the Great", 35 years, from 980 to 1015.
A note: "970 Fatimite caliphs established in Egypt."
Basil II and Constantine IX, 52 years; Bulgaria conquered 1018.
The heading "Rise of Seljukian Turks", about 1032.
Mahmoud, first sultan of Ghizni, conquers India.

entries.t: Round Tower at Newport, Rhode Island
entries.p: A drawing of the old stone tower with arches at Newport, Rhode Island.
King Canute, crowned, points while two courtiers listen. The caption reads "King Canute reproving his courtiers, 1020."
A heading: "8 Crusades or holy wars", with the note that a cross of red cloth on the right shoulder gave them the name "crusade."
Togrul Beg, who married the daughter of the caliph Kaim; a vast empire, 24 years.
Macbeth in the Scottish stream, slain by Macduff, ending in 1057.
Leo IX, the 155th pope, 6 years.
Edward the Confessor, son of Ethelred and Emma, reigned 24 years; the chart says he was followed by Harold II for 9 months in 1066.
A knight in armor dubs a kneeling young man with a sword. The caption says knighthood and chivalry existed from the 8th to the 15th century.
Alp Arslan, nephew, 11 years.
Two knights jousting on horseback. The caption says chivalry began in 912, that knights swore to be champions of God and the ladies, and that it flourished from the 11th to the 15th century.

A monk with a cross leads armed knights wearing red crosses. The caption says the First Crusade in 1096 was preached by Peter the Hermit, that its motto was "God wills it", and that the red cross on the shoulder (French croisade) gave it its name.
William the Conqueror of England, reigned 21 years and made many important changes; the Norman line begins in 1066.
Gregory VII, the 160th pope, 12 years (from 1073).
Red cross I, 1096 to 99: preached by Peter the Hermit in 1096; 300,000 men blessed by Urban II; Godfrey commanding; Jerusalem taken in 1099 and Godfrey made king.
Melek Shah, son: the highest pitch of splendor and power in his reign; 18 years.
A note that the right of investiture was settled by treaty between Pope Calixtus II and Emperor Henry V, at the 1st Lateran Council.
Urban II, the 162nd pope, 12 years; he blessed the First Crusade.
Red ring: the IXth Council, the 1st Lateran, March 18 to April 1123.
Red cross II, 1147-49: preached by St. Bernard in 1146, led by Conrad III and Louis VII, defeated. Jerusalem lost 1187.
A bar for Thomas Becket, high chancellor, who the chart says became Archbishop of Canterbury and was murdered (1170).
Red ring: the Xth Council, the 2nd Lateran, April 20, 1139.
The stream of the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem, 88 years, from 1099, with its kings Baldwin I, Baldwin II, Fulk of Anjou, Baldwin III, Almeric and four more.
An alphabetical table of peace treaties with their dates, from Abo (1743) to Westphalia (1648).
Saladin, 25 years; the note says Egypt took Palestine in 1187.
Portugal begins with Alfonso I, 57 years, declared king in 1139 after his victory over the Moors.

entries.t: Genghis Khan and the Mogul Empire
entries.p: The Moguls: the Mogul Empire founded by Genghis Khan, who the chart calls one of the most bloody conquerors of the world; the Tartars occupy the north of China.
Henry II, son of Maud, who married Plantagenet, Earl of Anjou; he conquered Ireland in October 1171 and reigned 35 years.
Frederick I, "Barbarossa", nephew; the most splendid reign in German history; drowned by his horse. 38 years.
Red cross III, 1189 to 92: Frederick Barbarossa, Philip II and Richard I; glorious but fruitless.
Red ring: the XIth Council, the 3rd Lateran, March 5-19, 1179.
A note: "Moscow built by George I, 1157."
Richard I, son, "Lion-hearted", reigned 10 years (1189-1199).
Red cross IV, 1195 to 97, under Henry VI.
John, "Lackland", who granted Magna Carta in 1215; reigned 17 years.
Innocent III, the 179th pope, 18 years (to 1216).
Red cross V, 1203: Baldwin, Count of Flanders, took Constantinople in 1203.
A magic lantern on a table. The caption says it was invented in 1260 by Roger Bacon, or by Athanasius Kircher, who died in 1680.
Red ring: the XIIth Council, the 4th Lateran, November 11-30, 1215.

entries.t: The Bible divided into chapters and verses
entries.p: An open Holy Bible between the dates 1227 and 1551. It says the Bible was divided into chapters by Cardinal Hugo in 1227 and into verses by Robert Stephens in 1551.
The stream note: Crusaders take Constantinople (1203); 5 French or Latin kings, 57 years.
A timber house with a thatched roof, dated 1240. The caption says houses in London were still thatched with straw then, with windows of lattice or paper and no chimneys.
Red cross VI, 1228: Emperor Frederick II took Jerusalem on a truce for 10 years (1229).
The Leaning Tower of Pisa beside its cathedral, dated 1154, with the note "188 feet high, and cathedral near by."
A man locked in a pillory before a crowd, dated 1256. The chart says the pillory was set up by law under Henry III in 1256 and abolished in 1837.

entries.t: Louis IX and the 7th and 8th Crusades
entries.p: Louis IX, son, who led the 7th Crusade in 1248 and the 8th in 1270 and died at Tunis; reigned 44 years.
Alexander Nevski, son, "the Saint", 18 years.
Red ring: the XIIIth Council at Lyons, June 28 to July 17, 1245.
Red cross VII, 1248 to 50: led by Louis IX, defeated and taken prisoner.
A bar for Roger Bacon, English philosopher, who the chart says invented spectacles and magnifying glasses; it gives him 80 years.
Red ring: the XIVth Council at Lyons, May 7 to June 17, 1274; the chart notes a temporary union of the Greek and Latin churches in 1274.
Michael Palaeologus, emperor of the Greek Empire, 22 years, from 1260 to 1282.
A note with a drawing of Windsor Castle, the home of the British kings. It says it was begun by William the Conqueror, enlarged by Henry I in 1110, and rebuilt by Edward III in 1356.
Kublai Kahn, 34 years, in the stream of China; the note says the Moguls had their capital in Pekin.
A note that Edward I defeated and killed Prince Llewellyn and subdued Wales in 1282, and made his eldest son "Prince of Wales", a title the eldest son has borne since.
Red cross VIII, 1270: Louis IX died at Carthage, followed by Edward I; Christians driven out of Syria in 1291.
Rudolph, Count of Hapsburg, 19 years from 1273.
A pair of spectacles. The chart says they were invented by Roger Bacon in 1280 (with a question mark), and also glass mirrors and magnifying glasses.
Edward I, "Longshanks", who conquered Wales in 1282, made his son Prince of Wales and had David, prince of Wales, drawn and quartered; reigned 35 years.
Boniface VIII, the 196th pope, 9 years.
A house with chimneys and glass windows, dated 1300. The caption says chimneys and window glass began to be used in London about 1300.

entries.t: Philip IV and the Babylonish Captivity
entries.p: Philip IV, "the Fair": the chart says the Pope was at Avignon from 1309 for 70 years, called the Babylonish Captivity of the Papal See.
A compass card dated 1302. The chart says the compass was known to the Chinese in 1115 BC (with a question mark), brought to Europe by Marco Polo in 1260 and improved by Flavio Gioja in 1302.

entries.t: Othman and the Ottoman Empire founded, 1299
entries.p: Othman, and the note "Ottoman Empire founded 1299."
Robert Bruce, king of Scotland, 23 years, from 1306.
Red ring: the XVth Council at Vienne, 1311-12; the Templars suppressed.

entries.t: Pope John XXII and the move to Avignon
entries.p: John XXII, the 199th pope, 19 years, with the papal tiara; the chart notes the purchase of Avignon.
A note that gunpowder was invented by M. Schwartz about 1320.
A note: "1348. 1,500,000 Jews massacred in Europe on suspicion of having poisoned the springs."
William Tell, "the Swiss patriot", aims his crossbow while a boy stands under a tree, dated 1306.
The Helvetic Confederacy of the Swiss cantons in 1307; Lucerne joins 1335, Zurich 1350.
A cannon on a wooden frame, dated 1308. The chart says cannon were used at Gibraltar in 1308, at Puy Guillaume in 1338 and by Philip VI at Crecy in 1346.
A Gothic clock dated 1348. The caption says the oldest clock known was put up in 1348 and is now in Dover Castle.
Orcan, son, 34 years, who conquers Lydia 1327, Mysia and Pergamos 1336, Phrygia 1338.
Edward III, son, reigned 50 years: a splendid reign with the victories of Crecy and Poitiers (1346 and 1356) and chivalry at its height.
A bar for John Wickliffe of Yorkshire, 60 years, ending in 1384; the chart notes he lived at the same time as Tamerlane.
A gun with the note that air-guns and muskets were invented about 1400.
An armored soldier firing a long hand gun. The caption says the culverin or hand cannon was used in 1378.
"Born, Timour or Tamerlane", 36 years, with his saying "As there is but one God in heaven, there should be but one master on earth."
A woman drawing water at a pump. The chart says pumps came into general use in England in 1425.

An open book labeled "Wickliffe's Bible, translated 1380". The chart says it existed only in handwritten copies for many years: the New Testament was not printed until 1731 or the Old Testament until 1848.
A playing card with the note that cards were invented in France in 1392 to amuse Charles VI during his bouts of madness.

entries.t: Union of Kalmar and Queen Margaret
entries.p: The Union of Calmar, 1397, under Margaret, "Semiramis of the North", 25 years.
Red ring: the XVIIth Council at Constance, 1414-18.
Charles VI, son, defeated at Agincourt in 1415 by Henry V of England, who was granted the succession at his death. Playing cards invented 1392.
Henry IV, cousin, with Shakespeare's line "Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown"; reigned 14 years (1399-1413).
Columbus at a table among Spanish nobles, standing an egg on its end.
Red ring: the XVIth Council at Pisa, 1409.
Henry V, son of Henry IV, in the English stream; the chart dates his reign from 1413 to 1422.
Gutenberg at his press holds a printed sheet reading "And there was light." The caption says he was born in 1400, died in 1468 and made the first movable types about 1440.
Martin V, the 211th pope, 15 years.
Joan of Arc in armor with a sword. The caption says she was burnt on May 31, 1431.

entries.t: Henry VI and the Wars of the Roses
entries.p: Henry VI, son, reigned 39 years; civil war of the white and red roses for 30 years (1455-85), Lancaster red, York white. His wife was Margaret of Anjou.

entries.t: Charles VII and Joan of Arc
entries.p: Charles VII, son, "the Victorious": the siege of Orleans was raised by Joan of Arc, May 8, 1429; reigned 39 years.
Red ring: the XVIIIth Council at Basle, 1439.
A note that tobacco was found at St. Domingo in 1492.
A pocket watch with the note that the first watch was made at Nuremberg in 1477.
Two figures showing dress: a French nobleman of 1540 and an English gentleman.
A red and a white rose with the note: thirty years' war of the white and red roses.
Constantine XIII, the last Greek emperor, falls in 1453, and Mohammed II, son, rules the Ottoman Empire 30 years.
Edward IV of the house of York; printing was introduced in England in 1471; succeeded by his son Edward for 74 days.
Sixtus IV, the 217th pope, 13 years.
A sailing ship off a coast, dated 1492. The caption says San Salvador was discovered on Friday, October 12, 1492.
A rider on a galloping horse carrying "News", captioned "1st post horses in 1481."
A portrait of Queen Isabella of Spain in a veil.
Isabella marries and unites her kingdom with Ferdinand's; "America discovered." 33 years.
A bar for the scholar Erasmus, from 1467, 69 years.
Henry VII, who married Queen Elizabeth, daughter of Edward IV; in 1488 the "Great Harry", the first ship of the Royal Navy, cost $70,000.
Alexander VI, the 219th pope, 11 years.
A bar for Cardinal Thomas Wolsey, from 1471, 59 years.
A bar for Raphael, painter, 37 years, from 1483 to 1520.
A bar for Copernicus of Thorn, Prussia, from 1473, 70 years.
A bar for Michael Angelo, architect of St. Peter's, 89 years.

entries.t: Babur founds the Mogul Empire of India
entries.p: Babour Mahommed, 47 years, who founded the Mogul Empire of Hindostan in 1525.
A woman seated at a spinning wheel, beside the caption that the spinning wheel was invented at Brunswick about 1530.
A portrait of Martin Luther standing in a dark robe, captioned "Martin Luther at Worms, 1521." His life bar below runs to his death in 1546 at age 63.

Henry VIII's reign in England, 38 years, with the fate of his six wives: Catharine divorced, Anne Boleyn beheaded, Jane Seymour died, Anne of Cleves divorced, Catharine Howard beheaded, Catharine Parr survived.
Francis I of France, "father of letters," who was at war with Charles V of Spain; he reigned 32 years.

entries.t: Henry VIII, head of the Church
entries.p: A crown with the words "Head of the Church, 1534," marking when Henry VIII made himself head of the church in England.
A green ring around the words "First Protestant creed, Augsburg, 1530, in Bavaria."
Charles I of Spain, who became king (emperor) of Germany in 1519 as Charles V, then gave up both crowns and retired to a monastery in 1556.

A diagram of the sun with the planets circling it, with their sizes and distances, beside the words: Copernicus teaches the true system of the revolution of the heavenly bodies, 1530. A bar below marks his life, 70 years, at Thorn in Prussia, to 1543.
Gustavus Vasa, king of Sweden from 1523, who reigned 37 years.
Solyman II, "the Magnificent," sultan of the Ottoman Empire, whose illustrious reign of 46 years the chart calls the august period of the empire.
A bar for John Knox of Scotland, the Reformer, who lived 67 years, to 1572.

A landscape of the New World under a caption: Columbus crossed the ocean in the Santa Maria, found San Salvador on October 12, 1492, and reached the mainland in 1498. The caption adds that 109 years passed before the first settlement at Jamestown, Virginia, in 1607.
A red ring marks the Council at Trent, 1545 to 1563, the 19th general council, on the stream of Papal Rome.
Ivan IV of Russia, "the Terrible," who reigned 51 years; the chart says he promoted trade but was cruel.

entries.t: Shakespeare reads his plays to Queen Elizabeth
entries.p: A scene of William Shakespeare standing with a book, reading his plays to Queen Elizabeth, who sits on a throne with a lady beside her.
A drawing of St. Peter's Basilica in Rome with its great dome, captioned "St. Peter's at Rome, commenced by Julius, 1506" (Pope Julius II).
In the block for Charles IX of France the chart notes the St. Bartholomew massacre of August 24, 1572.
Philip II of Spain, who reigned 42 years and married Mary, queen regent of England; the chart says he died a dreadful death covered with ulcers.
Queen Elizabeth of England, daughter of Anne Boleyn, who reigned 45 years.
Akbar of Hindostan (India), called illustrious and the greatest prince of India, who reigned 49 years.
An open book labeled "Bishops' Bible, 1568," the English Bible issued under Queen Elizabeth.
A bar for Lord Francis Bacon of England, who lived 65 years (1561 to 1626).

entries.t: Henry IV and the Edict of Nantes
entries.p: Henry IV of Bourbon, the first Bourbon king of France; the block notes the Edict of Nantes of April 13, 1598.

entries.t: Philip III drives out the Moors
entries.p: Philip III of Spain, who drove the Moors from Granada and nearby provinces in 1609.
A bar for James Usher (Ussher), Archbishop of Dublin, the scholar whose dates for the Bible this chart follows (Creation in 4004 BC).

entries.t: James I and the Bible translation
entries.p: King James I of England, crowned July 25, 1603; the block notes the Bible translated, the Gunpowder Plot and the Puritans leaving England.

entries.t: Ruins of the stone church at Jamestown
entries.p: A drawing of the ruined church tower at Jamestown, Virginia, the first lasting English settlement in America.
An open book labeled "Holy Bible, Authorized Version by King James, 1607 to 1611," the English translation made in those years.
Louis XIII of France, "the Just," whose prime minister was Cardinal Richelieu; the French Academy was organized in 1635.
Galileo, the celebrated astronomer, looks through a telescope he improved in 1610. Beside him are a thermometer (about 1600) and a note that he also found the steady swing of the pendulum (1635).
Michael, of the house of Romanoff, who began a reign of 32 years in Russia.

entries.t: William Harvey and the circulation of the blood
entries.p: A drawing of the human body with its blood vessels, and the text: William Harvey, M.D., of England discovers the circulation of the blood, 1619, with his explanation of the double work of the heart: sending blood out through the arteries and taking it back through the veins and the lungs.
King Charles I of England, called despotic, who was beheaded on January 30 after a reign of 24 years.
A bar for John Milton, English poet, who lived 66 years.
A bar for Spinoza of Amsterdam, who lived 45 years, 1632 to 1677.
A narrow block for the Commonwealth and Oliver Cromwell, between the reigns of Charles I and Charles II.

A drawing of the Gazetta of Venice, 1536, under the heading "First news papers," with a list: the Gazette de France 1631, the Public Intelligencer in England 1663, the Boston News Letter 1704 and the first newspaper in Germany 1715.
A bar for John Locke of England, who lived 72 years.
Charles II of England, called profligate; the block notes the plague of 1665 and the Great Fire (of London) in 1666.
Sir Isaac Newton sits under a tree; the caption says he discovered the power of gravity in 1666.
Louis XIV of France, who reigned 72 years; the block notes the Edict of Nantes revoked in 1685 and 500,000 Protestants exiled, and calls the reign renowned for literature and the arts.
Aurungzebe of India, whose illustrious reign of 49 years brought a huge yearly revenue.
A bar for William Penn, who received his grant (for Pennsylvania) in 1681 and lived 74 years, to 1718.
A line across the Germany stream: independence recognized in 1648 by the Treaty of Westphalia, and great quiet until the French Revolution.

Colored bars for the thirteen English colonies, each with its founding year and founders, starting with Virginia (1607), New York, Massachusetts (1620) and New Hampshire, and running up to the Revolution.
Kang-He of China, who reigned 62 years; the chart notes an earthquake in 1662 that killed 300,000 at Peking alone.
Peter the Great of Russia, its first emperor, who founded St. Petersburg in 1703 and reigned 43 years.
Ben Franklin flies a kite near a house; the text says he showed that lightning and electricity are the same in 1752, and that lightning rods came into use soon after.
A hot-air balloon, with the caption that Montgolfier raised the first balloon at Annonay, France, on June 5, 1783.
A bar for George Handel of Saxony, the composer, who lived 75 years.
A bar for Voltaire (Francois Arouet), who lived 84 years.

entries.t: James Watt and the power of steam
entries.p: A man watches a kettle boil by the fire; the caption says James Watt discovered the power of steam in 1750.
Frederick II of Prussia, "the Great," who reigned 46 years.

A stepped table of the states as they joined the United States after the thirteen colonies, from Vermont, Kentucky and Tennessee to California, Kansas, Nevada and Colorado (1876), with notes on who held each land before.
Maria Theresa of Austria, "a most noble queen," who reigned 40 years with her husband Francis I.
A horse-drawn coach, captioned "First mail by coaches, left London for Bristol, August 2, 1784."
A column marked "Revolution," 1775 to 1783 (8 years), where the colony bars end, followed by the years of the Confederation.
Catherine II of Russia, "a great sovereign," with a splendid reign; she was the wife of Peter III.
The Bunker Hill Monument, marking the battle of June 17, 1775, in the American Revolution.
A bar for Beethoven, who lived 57 years and lived in Vienna.
King George III of England; the block notes the American colonies lost in 1783, the Battle of Waterloo on June 18, 1815, and Napoleon banished in 1815.
A box camera on a tripod, captioned "First likeness by Daguerre, 1839."
A column for Napoleon Bonaparte, emperor of France, between the French Republic and the return of the Bourbon kings.
A paddle steamer under sail, captioned "First passenger steamboat, the Clermont, by Robert Fulton, on the Hudson River," 1807.
An open book labeled "The Book of Mormon" by Joseph Smith, the founding book of the Latter Day Saint movement.
Under Tippoo Saib the chart notes the English controlling India and the Sepoy mutiny at Vellore and later at Barrackpore and Delhi, May 10, 1857.
Columns for each president from Washington through Garfield, with their states, vice presidents and years in office, and notes such as the War of 1812 and the Mexican War.
A label across the president columns: the American Civil War, from April 12, 1861, to April 1865.
Louis Napoleon of France, president in 1848, emperor in 1852 and deposed in 1870.
The chart notes the first telegraph line in America, built by Professor Samuel F. B. Morse from Washington to Baltimore in 1844.
Queen Victoria of England, born May 24, 1819, daughter of Edward Duke of Kent and niece of William IV, with the line "God save the Queen."
A red ring in the papal stream around Pius IX and the 20th general council, the first Vatican council, which met December 8, 1869.
The column for Abraham Lincoln of Illinois, the 16th president; the words "American Civil War 1861 to 1865" run down beside it.
A steam engine pulling two cars, captioned "First steam railroad in 1830, from Baltimore to Ellicott's Mills."
Alexander II of Russia, son of Nicholas, assassinated March 13, 1881.

entries.t: The Revised Version of the Bible
entries.p: A note printed upright: the Revised Version of the New Testament was published May 17, 1881, and the revision of the Bible was begun in England on June 22, 1870.
A panel on the German Empire as a union of 4 kingdoms (Prussia, Wurtemberg, Bavaria, Saxony), 6 grand duchies, 5 duchies, 7 principalities, 3 towns and Alsace-Lorraine.
A list of the territories not yet states: the District of Columbia, Indian Territory, New Mexico, Utah, Washington, Dakota, Arizona, Idaho, Montana, Wyoming and Alaska.

entries.t: Portrait of Victoria, Queen of Eng
entries.p: An oval portrait of Queen Victoria of England, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Victoria, Queen of Eng.".

entries.t: Portrait of Grevy, Prest. of Fr. Republic
entries.p: An oval portrait of Jules Grevy, president of the French Republic, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Grevy, Prest. of Fr. Republic".

entries.t: Portrait of Leopold II, King of Belgium
entries.p: An oval portrait of Leopold II, king of Belgium, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Leopold II, King of Belgium".

entries.t: Portrait of Francis Joseph, Empr. of Aus
entries.p: An oval portrait of Francis Joseph, emperor of Austria, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Francis Joseph, Empr. of Aus.".

entries.t: Portrait of William I, Empr. of Ger
entries.p: An oval portrait of William I, emperor of Germany, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "William I, Empr. of Ger.".

entries.t: Portrait of Oscar II, King of Sweden
entries.p: An oval portrait of Oscar II, king of Sweden, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Oscar II, King of Sweden".

entries.t: Portrait of Alfonso XII, King of Spain
entries.p: An oval portrait of Alfonso XII, king of Spain, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Alfonso XII, King of Spain".

entries.t: Portrait of Humbert I, King of Italy
entries.p: An oval portrait of Humbert (Umberto) I, king of Italy, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Humbert I, King of Italy".

entries.t: Portrait of Nasr-ul-Deen, Shah of Per
entries.p: An oval portrait of Nasr-ul-Deen, shah of Persia, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Nasr-ul-Deen, Shah of Per.".
An oval portrait of George Washington, the 1st president of the United States, captioned "Gen. Geo. Washington" with the dates born 1732, died 1799.
An oval portrait of James K. Polk, the 11th president of the United States, captioned "Jas. K. Polk" with the dates born 1795, died 1849.

entries.t: Principal Reigning Sovereigns of the World
entries.p: The heading over a panel of oval portraits of the rulers reigning when the chart was made, from Queen Victoria and the German emperor to the pope, the sultan of Turkey and the emperors of China and Japan.

entries.t: Portrait of Frederick, Grand Duke of Baden
entries.p: An oval portrait of Frederick, grand duke of Baden, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Frederick, Gr.-D. of Baden".

entries.t: Portrait of Charles I, King of Wurtemberg
entries.p: An oval portrait of Charles I, king of Wurtemberg, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Charles I, King of Wurtemberg".

entries.t: Portrait of Ludwig II, King of Bavaria
entries.p: An oval portrait of Ludwig II, king of Bavaria, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Ludwig II, King of Bavaria".

entries.t: Portrait of John, King of Saxony
entries.p: An oval portrait of John, king of Saxony, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "John, King of Saxony".

entries.t: Portrait of Alexander II, Late Czar of Rus
entries.p: An oval portrait of Alexander II, the late czar of Russia, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Alexander II, Late Czar of Rus.".

entries.t: Portrait of Alexander III, Czar of Rus
entries.p: An oval portrait of Alexander III, czar of Russia, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Alexander III, Czar of Rus.".

entries.t: Portrait of Dom Pedro II, Empr. of Brazil
entries.p: An oval portrait of Dom Pedro II, emperor of Brazil, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Dom Pedro II, Empr. of Brazil".
An oval portrait of Pope Leo XIII, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Pope Leo XIII".

entries.t: Portrait of Abdul-Hamid, Sultan of Tur
entries.p: An oval portrait of Abdul-Hamid (II), sultan of Turkey, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Abdul-Hamid, Sultan of Tur.".

entries.t: Portrait of Moutz Hito, Mikado of Japan
entries.p: An oval portrait of Moutz Hito (Mutsuhito), the mikado (emperor) of Japan, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Moutz Hito, Mikado of Japan".
An oval portrait of John Adams, the 2nd president of the United States, captioned "John Adams" with the dates born 1735, died 1826.
An oval portrait of Zachary Taylor, the 12th president of the United States, captioned "Gen. Z. Taylor" with the dates born 1784, died 1850.
An oval portrait of the Prince of Wales (later King Edward VII), one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Prince of Wales".

entries.t: Portrait of Gambetta, Prest. Fr. Cham. Dep
entries.p: An oval portrait of Leon Gambetta, president of the French Chamber of Deputies, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Gambetta, Prest. Fr. Cham. Dep.".

entries.t: Portrait of William III, King of Hol
entries.p: An oval portrait of William III, king of Holland, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "William III, King of Hol.".

entries.t: Portrait of Crown Prince of Aus
entries.p: An oval portrait of the crown prince of Austria (Rudolf), one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Crown Prince of Aus.".

entries.t: Portrait of Crown Prince of Ger
entries.p: An oval portrait of the crown prince of Germany (later Emperor Frederick III), one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Crown Prince of Ger.".

entries.t: Portrait of Christian IX, King of Den
entries.p: An oval portrait of Christian IX, king of Denmark, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Christian IX, King of Den.".

entries.t: Portrait of Louis I, King of Port
entries.p: An oval portrait of Louis (Luis) I, king of Portugal, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Louis I, King of Port.".

entries.t: Portrait of George I, King of Greece
entries.p: An oval portrait of George I, king of Greece, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "George I, King of Greece".

entries.t: Portrait of Tsae-Teen, Emp. of China
entries.p: An oval portrait of Tsae-Teen (the Guangxu Emperor), emperor of China, one of the principal reigning sovereigns of the world at the time of the chart, captioned "Tsae-Teen, Emp. of China".
An oval portrait of Thomas Jefferson, the 3rd president of the United States, captioned "Thomas Jefferson" with the dates born 1743, died 1826.
An oval portrait of Millard Fillmore, the 13th president of the United States, captioned "Millard Fillmore" with the dates born 1800, died 1874.
An oval portrait of James Madison, the 4th president of the United States, captioned "James Madison" with the dates born 1751, died 1836.
An oval portrait of Franklin Pierce, the 14th president of the United States, captioned "Franklin Pierce" with the dates born 1804, died 1869.

entries.t: Presidents of the United States: chronological table of events
entries.p: A long dated list of events in United States history, from the founding of St. Augustine, Florida, in 1565 through the Revolution, the War of 1812, the Mexican War and the Civil War.
An oval portrait of James Monroe, the 5th president of the United States, captioned "James Monroe" with the dates born 1758, died 1831.
